basis: May is the shortest bar on the shared kWh scale, with its top below the 10,000 tick (~8,000–8,500 kWh), while the next-lowest month (Jun) is ~17,500 kWh; May is less than half the height of the next-lowest bar and dramatically lower than all other months. No explicit numeric threshold separating 'standard' from 'critical' is printed, so the decision rests on the magnitude of the relative deviation. A drop to less than half the next-lowest month and far below the mid-range cluster (~20,000–30,000 kWh) is an extreme, isolated low-output value, not a routine dip. This supports treating May as a critical low-output anomaly rather than a standard low-output case. Residual limit: no formal policy threshold is supplied, so the 'critical' classification is based on the pronounced relative deviation visible on the dashboard.
option_label: Escalate May to critical low-output anomaly review
